claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can refine the inherited lamellar microstructure of an AlCoCrFeNi2.1-like eutectic high-entropy alloy into an ultrafine-grained duplex structure.
Cryo-rolling followed by optimized annealing will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
The as-cast eutectic alloy has a naturally occurring duplex lamellar microstructure.
The FCC constituent is relatively soft and ductile, whereas the BCC constituent is relatively hard and prone to brittleness.
The hard constituent in the target lamellar alloy may instead be a B2 or other intermetallic phase.
Cryo-rolling induces severe deformation, high dislocation density, and grain refinement in the target eutectic alloy.
Controlled annealing after rolling restores ductility and promotes a heterogeneous ultrafine-grained duplex lamellar structure.
The proposed improvement should hold during quasi-static room-temperature testing of alloys compositionally similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The treatment produces an ultrafine-grained duplex lamellar structure with a high density of phase boundaries.
Phase boundaries impede dislocation motion and microcrack propagation.
Post-rolling annealing balances recovery against controlled phase coarsening.
Hierarchical structural heterogeneity and microcrack arrest improve the mechanical response of the processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy.
Dislocation storage, microcrack arrest, and more uniform local stress distribution enhance strain hardening and thereby improve both strength and ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–50% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will maintain or modestly enhance ductility relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast baseline has coarser lamellae than the thermo-mechanically processed material.
The as-cast baseline has less effective load transfer at phase boundaries, causing a strength–ductility compromise.
The improvement is primarily limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with a distinct dual-phase lamellar architecture.
The exact property changes and optimal rolling reduction, cryogenic temperature, annealing temperature, and annealing time remain experimentally undetermined.
A controlled comparison of identically composed processed and as-cast samples using tensile testing and electron microscopy can test the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis says ductility will increase, whereas the predicted outcome permits ductility merely to be maintained.
The treatment is called 'single-step,' but it explicitly consists of two sequential processing stages: cryo-rolling and annealing.

The hypothesis requires simultaneous strength and ductility improvement, but the stated falsification rule uses a joint condition, so strength improvement accompanied by deteriorated ductility would not necessarily falsify it.
